interview.answer: Designing layouts that adapt to different screen sizes, orientations and input methods using flexible grids, images and media queries.
Writing base styles for small screens and adding complexity with min-width media queries for larger ones.
Writing base styles for large screens and overriding with max-width media queries for smaller ones.
It starts with the smallest, most constrained layout and enhances progressively, which is easier to maintain.
A CSS rule that applies styles only when the device or viewport matches a condition such as width or orientation.

interview.q: What is the viewport meta tag?
interview.answer: It tells the browser to set the layout viewport width to the device width and initial scale to 1.

interview.q: Why is the viewport meta tag necessary?
interview.answer: Without it, mobile browsers assume a desktop-width viewport and zoom out, breaking responsive layouts.
A viewport width at which the layout changes to better fit the available space.

interview.q: Should breakpoints be based on devices or content?
interview.answer: Content; choose widths where the layout breaks, not specific device sizes, so it stays future-proof.
A layout that uses relative units and flexible containers so it adapts continuously instead of jumping at breakpoints.
It constrains a value between a minimum and maximum, useful for fluid typography and spacing.

interview.q: How do you make fluid type?
interview.answer: Use font-size: clamp(1rem, 0.5rem + 1vw, 2rem) so text scales smoothly between bounds.
A viewport-relative unit equal to 1% of the viewport width.
A viewport-relative unit equal to 1% of the viewport height.
A dynamic viewport height unit that accounts for mobile browser chrome appearing and disappearing.

interview.q: Why use dvh instead of vh on mobile?
interview.answer: vh includes the area under the browser UI, causing layout jumps; dvh adjusts as the UI shows or hides.

interview.q: What is an aspect-ratio media feature?
interview.answer: It matches the ratio of width to height of the viewport.
A media feature that matches when the viewport is wider than it is tall.
A media feature that detects whether the user prefers a light or dark colour scheme.
A media feature that detects whether the user wants reduced animation, used to disable motion.

interview.q: How do you make images responsive?
interview.answer: Set max-width: 100% and height: auto, and use srcset and sizes for different resolutions.
An HTML attribute listing image sources with widths so the browser picks the best one.
It tells the browser the display size of the image at each breakpoint so it can choose from srcset.
It lets you provide multiple sources with media queries, such as art-directed images or modern formats.
A container with a max-width and auto margins, so it centres and stops growing on large screens.
A function that returns the smaller of two values, useful for responsive sizing.
A function that returns the larger of two values, useful for enforcing minimum sizes.
A grid using fr units and auto-fit/minmax so columns reflow without media queries.
A query that applies styles based on a container's size rather than the viewport.
They let components respond to their own available space, making them reusable in different layouts.
The at-rule that defines a container query.
It establishes a container for size queries, such as inline-size.
It names a container so queries can target it specifically.
A table that scrolls horizontally or reflows into cards on small screens to avoid overflow.

interview.q: What is overflow-x: auto on a table wrapper?
interview.answer: It lets a wide table scroll horizontally instead of breaking the page layout.
It controls how touch gestures are handled, such as pan and pinch, to avoid conflicts with custom interactions.
It prevents mobile browsers from automatically inflating text size in landscape mode.

interview.q: What is a responsive navigation pattern?
interview.answer: A nav that collapses into a menu on small screens, often with a toggle button.
A button with three lines that toggles a collapsed navigation on small screens.

interview.q: What is the risk of hiding navigation behind a hamburger?
interview.answer: Discoverability drops; ensure the toggle is accessible and the menu is keyboard-navigable.

interview.q: What is srcset with x descriptors?
interview.answer: It provides images for different device pixel ratios, such as 1x and 2x.

interview.q: What is the difference between w and x descriptors in srcset?
interview.answer: w describes width in pixels; x describes device pixel ratio.
Spacing that scales with the viewport, such as margin using clamp or vw.

interview.q: What is the difference between em and vw for responsive spacing?
interview.answer: em tracks font size; vw tracks viewport width, so they respond to different changes.

interview.q: What is a breakpoint-less responsive design?
interview.answer: A design that adapts fluidly using clamp, minmax and flex/grid without explicit media queries.
